tasks.short: Explain repayment options and help customers choose practical next actions.

steps.what: Review balances, payments, disputes and earlier collection activity.
Check repayment rules and calculate permitted instalment examples.
Discuss constraints, explain options and agree practical next actions.
Write and send a summary of advice and next actions.

loop.input: Collector's brief notes, agreed advice and validated repayment figures.
loop.output: Plain-language advice confirmation with source-linked figures.
loop.check: Code checks amounts and dates; collector checks meaning, tone and absence of unapproved commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction maximum; missing agreement or failed checks return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard schedules; varied customer explanations require limited free-text drafting.

steps.what: Record the advice and set the next contact date.

tasks.design: An integration brings {ERP} balances and {CRM} history into one account brief; deterministic code calculates examples from approved rules in {DOCS}. The collector gives advice, approves a bounded draft before {EMAIL} delivery, and lets configured {CRM} workflows record the outcome and schedule follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account history and policy sit in separate places. Customer explanations make complete scripts brittle.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and workflow features handle retrieval and follow-up. AI-assisted coding makes the small calculator and connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A permitted schedule may still be unaffordable. Disputed debt, vulnerability and concessions require judgement and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without pressure, distinguish inability from confusion, and explain options without promising an unsuitable arrangement.
tasks.altitude: The collector spends less time assembling facts and writing summaries. A proposed delegation lets them arrange payment-date changes within explicit limits; concessions still follow existing approval rights.

reach.task: Review requests for exceptions to standard repayment terms.
reach.learn: Assess cash-flow evidence, distinguish advice from credit decisions, and document reasons for escalation.

evidence.claim: Dunning workflows, reminders and call campaigns are available capabilities; personalised repayment advice remains a separate design.
Policy-based schedule calculations and approved-note drafting are feasible without autonomous negotiation; effort estimates are provisional.
GDPR requires appropriate access, data minimisation and retention controls for customer account information.

assumptions: The typical setting uses the {ERP} for receivables, the {CRM} for collection history and telephone contact for advice.
Repayment rules can be expressed as limits, dates and calculations; the calculator does not infer personal affordability.
Shares are reasoned estimates. Human advice remains the largest step despite the prior probability of extensive automation.
Estimates cover one receivables entity, one language and existing interfaces. Access and consultation ranges include work where required, not guaranteed elapsed approval times.
Advice, persuasion and overdue-payment diagnosis can occur in one call; savings across these tasks must not be added without measuring overlap.
unknowns: Customer mix: businesses, consumers or both.
Approved repayment rules and the collector's actual authority.
Available interfaces, account identifiers and data freshness.
Applicable national collection rules and whether employee consultation is required.
Whether existing software already provides schedule calculations and outcome logging.
research_questions: Which advice confirmations fit deterministic templates?
Where do customers misunderstand instalment amounts, dates or consequences?
Does the proposed use fall within any EU AI Act creditworthiness provisions? Classification depends on intended use.
new_work: Maintain repayment rules, templates and escalation contacts.
Handle missing account data and failed synchronisation.
Check that summaries contain no unsupported commitments or unnecessary sensitive details.

tasks.short: Investigate account problems and explain balances, payments and corrections to customers.

steps.what: Receive the question and verify the customer's identity and account access.
Retrieve invoices, payment allocations and earlier correspondence.
Compare the customer's explanation with account records and identify the discrepancy.

loop.input: Verified question, relevant correspondence and a bounded set of account transactions.
loop.output: Proposed discrepancy category, supporting records and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Code verifies arithmetic and transaction references; collector confirms the interpretation before use.
loop.stop: One analysis and one correction maximum; contradictory evidence or uncertain ownership goes to manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Amounts reconcile deterministically, but customer explanations and correspondence do not consistently use transaction identifiers.

steps.what: Choose an explanation or refer a correction request to the responsible team.
Explain the finding and tell the customer what happens next.

loop.input: Approved finding, verified figures and the current correction-request status.
loop.output: Suggested spoken explanation or written response.
loop.check: Every amount and status must match a source; collector approves content before speaking or sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision maximum; disputes, distress or unsupported claims return to personal handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover balance questions; varied problem explanations sometimes need a short tailored draft.

steps.what: Record the answer and track any outstanding correction.

tasks.design: A configured inquiry form in {CRM} retrieves authorised records from {ERP} and relevant {EMAIL} threads. Code reconciles amounts, while bounded loops propose discrepancy summaries and explanations for collector approval; {WORKFLOW} tracks correction requests without making financial adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invoices, allocations and customer explanations use different references. Staff reconstruct the same history across screens and correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic reconciliation and account links already exist in many systems. Small connectors and bounded text interpretation can fill the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Unallocated payments, disputed charges and delayed corrections can leave several plausible explanations. A readable draft cannot establish that a debt is valid.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a real dispute, take ownership of the customer's problem and avoid treating an unresolved correction as refusal to pay.
tasks.altitude: The collector spends more time resolving causes and less time searching records. They can prioritise correction requests within a proposed service mandate; refund and write-off authority does not automatically expand.

reach.task: Investigate recurring invoice errors before the next billing cycle.
reach.learn: Understand invoice adjustments, allocation rules and the evidence required for a correction.

reach.task: Report dispute causes and correction delays.
reach.learn: Define consistent cause categories and distinguish open cases from confirmed billing errors.

evidence.claim: Bank lines can be matched using payment references, account identifiers or invoice numbers, with exceptions handled by people.
The digest does not establish automated resolution of account disputes; source-linked explanations and the time shares are design estimates.
GDPR requires preventing disclosure of account information to unauthorised recipients.

assumptions: Telephone inquiries are common; written inquiries use the same evidence and resolution flow.
Identity verification remains explicit. Existing verified-channel context reduces repeated checks where policy permits.
Financial adjustments are separate controlled actions performed by the responsible team.
The automation prior is plausible for simple questions, but mixed disputes retain meaningful human investigation and response time.
Ranges cover one inquiry queue and existing interfaces; required employee consultation and access preparation are included in consent_and_access.
unknowns: Share of simple balance questions versus disputed charges.
Identity-verification policy for each channel.
Whether invoices, bank allocations and correspondence share reliable account identifiers.
Correction approval rights and response times.
Existing inquiry features in the {CRM} and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which discrepancy categories can be resolved entirely with deterministic checks?
How often do payment-feed delays produce incorrect collection explanations?
Does a source-linked draft reduce handling time without increasing repeat contacts?
new_work: Review discrepancy summaries and customer responses.
Maintain inquiry categories and correction-routing rules.
Resolve unmatched identifiers and stale source records.
Sample answers for unsupported figures, incorrect status and disclosure errors.

tasks.short: Negotiate payment or merchandise return and follow through on agreed commitments.

steps.what: Select overdue accounts for today's collection contacts.
Check balances, disputes, contact history and permitted settlement or return terms.
Contact the customer and negotiate payment or merchandise return.
Approve or reject requested concessions beyond the collector's authority.
Confirm approved payment dates, amounts or return arrangements with the customer.
Record commitments and schedule checks for payment or return completion.

tasks.design: Configured {CRM} workflows build contact queues from {ERP} ageing, recent payments and dispute holds, then present approved settlement rules from {DOCS}. People negotiate and approve exceptions; templates produce gated confirmations, while {CRM} tracks commitments against {ERP} payments and {OPS_SYSTEM} return status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Negotiation was treated as one indivisible human task. Preparation, concession requests and commitment tracking remained attached to it.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing dunning configuration can handle queues and reminders. Small integrations can supply fresh balances and return status without modelling persuasion.
tasks.still_hard: Obtaining a credible commitment, responding to hardship and deciding concessions remain human work. Contact restrictions and enforcement rules vary nationally.
tasks.human_edge: Earn cooperation, recognise pressure or distress, and judge whether an offer is realistic and fair.
tasks.altitude: The collector spends more of the week negotiating and rescuing failed arrangements. They gain control over follow-up timing within contact rules; settlement limits require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Review failed payment arrangements and propose changes to settlement limits.
reach.learn: Compare recovery outcomes, customer harm and the costs of repeated unsuccessful contact.

evidence.claim: Dunning workflows support reminders, letters and call campaigns.
Negotiation, payment plans and enforcement decisions remain human responsibilities in the digest's proposed approach.
A deterministic commitment tracker can compare agreed dates and amounts with posted payments; estimates require local validation.

assumptions: The typical workload mainly concerns overdue invoices; merchandise returns apply only where the business supplies goods.
The exception-approval share is averaged across all cases; most contacts need no manager approval.
Contact ranking uses explicit ageing, amount and promise-date rules, without inferred personal creditworthiness.
This task ends with commitment tracking. It does not initiate disconnection, repossession or legal proceedings.
The low prior for full automation fits the human negotiation and concession steps.
Ranges assume existing collection features and include access preparation and employee consultation where required.
unknowns: Existing contact limits, dispute holds and settlement mandates.
Whether payment and return feeds are timely enough to suppress inappropriate follow-up.
Frequency of concessions requiring manager approval.
Applicable national collection rules and third-party collection requirements.
Whether the collector's current system already tracks promises and failed commitments.
research_questions: Which queue rules reduce unnecessary contact while preserving recovery?
What distinguishes broken promises caused by processing delays from genuine non-payment?
Which agreement types fit existing confirmation templates without free-text generation?
new_work: Maintain contact suppression and settlement rules.
Review proposed confirmations and exceptional concessions.
Resolve late feeds and false broken-promise alerts.
Check complaint patterns and outcomes after changing contact timing.

tasks.short: Discuss overdue payments with customers and clarify relevant contract terms.

steps.what: Review overdue invoices, payments and previous contact before speaking.
Find the signed contract and check relevant payment or service terms.

loop.input: Linked signed contract and amendments, limited to payment and relevant service clauses.
loop.output: Clause excerpts with document version, page references and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Each excerpt must match its source; collector verifies the effective version and relevant amendments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry maximum; missing signatures, conflicting versions or ambiguous clauses go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use structured clause fields where available; varied legacy documents require bounded extraction.

steps.what: Ask why payment is overdue and discuss the relevant contract terms.
Write the contact record and classify the overdue-payment reason.

loop.input: Brief collector-entered notes and an approved reason-code list.
loop.output: Proposed reason code and concise contact record.
loop.check: Collector confirms factual accuracy; sensitive details are omitted unless necessary and permitted.
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction maximum; unclear reasons remain unknown rather than inferred.
loop.why_not_simpler: A dropdown handles simple cases; mixed free-text explanations need a bounded classification proposal.

steps.what: Send the agreed action or dispute to the responsible colleague.

tasks.design: A shared account view combines {ERP} and {CRM} records with source-linked clauses from {CLM} or {DOCS}. The conversation stays with the collector; a bounded loop proposes the contact record and reason code for approval, then {WORKFLOW} routes agreed actions and disputes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contract versions are difficult to locate, and conversation records are free text. The human conversation obscured opportunities to improve preparation and routing.
tasks.enabler_now: Document links and deterministic retrieval handle known contracts. Bounded extraction and classification can assist with legacy documents and brief notes.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may reveal the real cause only after trust develops. Conflicting amendments, disputed terms and sensitive personal circumstances require careful human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Ask tactful follow-up questions, notice uncertainty and distinguish a contractual misunderstanding from hardship or a genuine dispute.

ambition.what: Weekly review of recurring contract-term misunderstandings.

tasks.altitude: The collector arrives better prepared and spends less time documenting calls. They can initiate evidence-backed billing or contract-clarity reviews, while contract changes remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Review recurring complaints about collection explanations and contract terms.
reach.learn: Recognise conduct issues, preserve relevant evidence and apply escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Correct invoice wording that repeatedly causes payment misunderstandings.
reach.learn: Trace contract terms into invoice presentation and distinguish confirmed defects from customer allegations.

evidence.claim: Collection software supports call campaigns and workflow preparation; this does not establish automated debt conversations.
Source-linked clause extraction and classification of brief notes are feasible bounded loops; their accuracy and savings need local testing.
The EU AI Act lists worker monitoring and natural-person creditworthiness among high-risk uses; intended purpose determines relevance here.
GDPR and applicable national rules govern sensitive notes, access and retention. Recording calls would require a separate assessment.

assumptions: Telephone is the main channel; occasional personal visits retain the same human conversation step.
Signed contracts are held in the {CLM} or {DOCS}; smaller organisations may use only the {DOCS}.
The design uses collector-entered notes and does not require call recording.
Clause extraction supports explanation; it does not determine legal enforceability.
The strong conversation prior fits this decomposition. Preparation and paperwork still offer useful savings.
Ranges cover one contract family initially; access and consultation work includes employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether contracts and amendments can be linked reliably to customer accounts.
Share of standard contracts versus individually negotiated terms.
Permitted reason categories and retention periods for sensitive explanations.
National consultation requirements and any intended use of contact records for staff monitoring.
Who owns billing disputes, contractual interpretation and hardship referrals.
research_questions: How often does contract-version uncertainty delay a customer discussion?
Which reason codes lead to distinct, useful follow-up actions?
Can brief structured notes provide enough evidence without storing unnecessary personal information?
new_work: Verify extracted clauses and effective contract versions.
Approve contact records and reason codes.
Maintain routing rules and resolve unowned referrals.
Review recurring misunderstandings without turning customer notes into unsupported staff-performance scores.

role.altitude: The week shifts from searching, retyping and chasing internal updates toward customer conversations, dispute resolution and failed-arrangement recovery. Greater settlement or correction authority requires explicit delegation; automation alone grants none.
reach: Billing clerks: jointly remove recurring invoice defects.
Credit analysts: prepare evidence for repayment exceptions.
Compliance officers: identify recurring conduct and contract-explanation issues.
Business intelligence analysts: turn confirmed dispute causes into useful operational reporting.
skills_to_grow: Empathetic negotiation and recognition of customer vulnerability.
Payment allocation, invoice correction and contract-version checking.
Verification of source-linked drafts and bounded model outputs.
GDPR data minimisation and EU AI Act literacy appropriate to the intended use.
role.ambitious_version: A collector who resolves the causes of late payment, offers earlier planning support and brings evidence to billing and credit-policy decisions, while keeping sensitive negotiations and consequential approvals with authorised people.
